segments.text: Good afternoon, this is Aakashwani and I am Sairam Uchthaba with the Mid-Day News.
The Headlines
Prime Minister Narendra Modi urges people to buy products made by local artisans during the
festive season to strengthen vocal for local and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Prime Minister Modi in
his Man ki Baat program on Aakashwani says, East Sanjeevni has facilitated nearly 50 crore
teleconsultations, improving access to healthcare in remote areas and making people's lives
easier.
Prime Minister says the supportive ecosystem in the country is helping startups develop
innovative deep-tech solutions, including application of artificial intelligence.
Prime Minister highlights advances in brain research at IIT Madras, stresses the importance
of organ donation in saving lives and advancing medical research.
Mr. Modi attends Air Force hosted wings over Ganges Air Show in Varanasi, also to inaugurate
RBI Data Center in Bhubaneshwar this evening.
India slams Pakistan at UN on Minority Rights violations and military control, reaffirms
J&K's integral part of India.
And in French open badminton championship, two-time Olympic medalist PV Sindhu to take
on South Korea's World No. 1 R.C. Young in Women's Singles final this afternoon.
And now the news in detail. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said,
Man ki Baat has completed 12 years and that the journey has felt like a pilgrimage for
him. Addressing the nation through his Man ki Baat program on Akashwani, the Prime Minister
noted that Man ki Baat began on the auspicious occasion of Vijaya Dashmi 12 years ago.
So, since then, this journey has continued without a break.
Mr. Modi Adrin, that this has been like a tirthyatra or pilgrimage to closely understand
the efforts of the people and to salute their contributions.
The Prime Minister noted that Glen and his drives are being run at many places ahead
of festivals like Diwali and Chhat. He stressed the need to maintain cleanliness of the places
where people live. He added that small individual efforts can bring about significant change
in the surroundings. Mr Modi expressed happiness that on Gandhi Jayanthi this year, sales of
products of Ghadi Gramudyo crossed 28 crore rupees in a single day. This is an increase
of 1.5 crore rupees over last year. He said the popularity of Ghadi continues to grow
and benefits are reaching the people who bring Kadi and various handicrafts to life.
Mr. Modi urged people to prioritize products made by local artisans during the festive season.
He added that this will further strengthen the vocal for local movement
and the dream of Atma Nirbhar Bharat will be realized sooner.
Speaking about the E. Sanjeevani scheme, Prime Minister Modi expressed satisfaction that
approximately 50 crore teleconcertations have been conducted through this platform so far
to make people's lives easier.
I am very happy to see that up to now,
nearly 50 crore tele-consultations have been done.
The power of technology has been served by our doctors
and it is an excellent example of the country's trust.
Today, through our special network,
we have reached far-away areas of the country.
Recalling his trip to Chennai earlier this month, Mr. Modi said he met many of the nation's
scientists, researchers and young talents.
He said the nation's youth are currently working on subjects that have the potential
to transform the future of humanity.
He cited brain research as one such field.
Mr. Modi had inaugurated the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Center at IIT Madras.
The goal is to map the 3D of 100 human brains in the coming days and focus on their details.
This is the first mission in the world.
In this work, the traditional super-computer is being used.
Even today, there are diseases like Alzheimer's and dementia.
Touching upon the subject of organ donation, Prime Minister Modi said it plays a vital role
in such advanced research.
He gave the example of Shivani from Narmadaapuram in Madhya Pradesh, who had met with a road
accident and her family decided to donate her organs. Mr. Modi praised her family,
saying such a step of humanity can bring happiness back into a family's life while
also providing significant support to research efforts.
The Prime Minister also shared some other experiences from his visit to Chennai.
The first was his interaction with young people on the metro while another was his
visit to IIT Madras. Mr. Modi highlighted that one of the startups he saw focuses on
verifying the quality of gold which can help prevent fraud in gold purchases.
He added that another team is developing a platform that could enable the rapid recovery
of funds lost to bank fraud.
He further said that another team is exploring how AI can assist in screening of cervical
cancer.
Mr. Vodhi said that the interaction at IIT was entirely focused on deep tech.
These startups are being supported by the incubation ecosystem at IIT Madras.
These start-ups are getting help from the IIT Madras Incubation Ecosystem.
One of these start-ups is developing an electric vehicle on the ocean.
Another start-up is creating fast-charging batteries for drone and electric vehicles.
One team is working on the use of AI in defense technology.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is attending the third and final day of the mega air show
Wings Over Ganges at Namukhat in Varanasi today as the chief guest.
The event was organized to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force.
Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh are also present at
the event.
The Air Force Day Aerial Display 2026 held at Namukh Heart offered a spectacular showcase
of the Indian Air Force's prowess and valor.
The sky resonated with the raw of combat aircraft such as the Tejas, the light combat
helicopter Prachand, Chetak, Chinook and Rafal.
as well. Transport aircrafts also participated in the air show.
Earlier, the Prime Minister inaugurated a new textile manufacturing facility in Varanasi.
The Prime Minister also interacted with the female staff there. Chief Minister Yogi Adyatnath
and Governor Anandi Ben Patel were also present at the event. This facility marks an important
step towards strengthening India's textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promoting
industrial growth in the region.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Data Centre and
Cyber Security Training Institute at Jattani near Bhuvaneshwar in Odisha this evening.
Our correspondent reports that the facility is expected to strengthen data security
and enhance the resilience of India's digital financial infrastructure.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.

Inter-criticized Pakistan at the United Nations, accusing Islamabad of attempting
to malign New Delhi through propaganda while diverting attention from its domestic
challenges, including economic distress, lawlessness, and human rights violations.
Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the special rapporteur on minority issues at
the UN General Assembly's third committee yesterday, India's first secretary to the
UN, Raghu Puri, questioned Pakistan's record on minority rights and alleged that the
country's military continued to exercise decisive control over its political leadership.
Puri also highlighted concerns over the shrinking minority population in Pakistan, and urged
Islamabad to focus on the welfare of its own citizens rather than criticizing India at
international forums.
From Khaybat-Pakhtunkhwa to Balochistan, it is well documented that Pakistan's minorities
have shrunk dramatically since its independence.
As far as Jammu and Kashmir is concerned, it is an integral and inalienable part of
India, and the only question that remains is the vacation of the region illegally occupied
ride by Pakistan.
The Intel Meteorological Department, IMD, has said that the depression over east-central
and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal has moved southeastwards and lay-centred about
440 kilometers north-northwest of Sri Vijayapuram in Andhra Mananikoba Islands and 880 kilometers
east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.
It is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and
to a severe cyclonic storm over West Central Bay of Bengal around Tuesday morning.
Talking to Akashwari News, Director-General of IMT Dr. Mritian J. Mohapatra said,
Due to influence of depression, the sea condition is very rough and will deteriorate further.

So therefore, people should be cussed.
Fishermen should not go into the sea.
Those who are out at sea should return to the coast immediately.
Shipping operations should be regulated.
There will be total suspension of fishing operation.
The coastal population living in the lowland areas should be cussed
and they should stay in safe place on 28th of October.
Odisha has stepped up cyclone preparedness
as the weather system of the Bay of Bengal
call is forecast to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and across the Andhra
Pradesh coast on Wednesday.
The state government has kept 302 rescue teams ready and ordered the closure of educational
institutions in five southern districts on Wednesday and Thursday.
A report.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast maximum sustained winds of 115 to 125 kilometers
per hour, gusting to 140 kilometers per hour during landfall.
The IMD has predicted widespread impact of this very severe cyclonic storm on
southern and some coastal districts of Odisha, schools, colleges and Anganwadi centers in
Ganjam, Gajapati, Raigada, Koraput and Valkangiri will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday.
Farmers face the risk of paddy lodging, waterlogging and damage to standing vegetables. Authorities
are focusing on crop protection and the rapid restoration of essential services.
Prakash Das for KASVANI NEWS, Bhuvaneswar
On to sports now. In the French open badminton championship, two-time Olympic
medalist P.B. Sindhu will take on South Korea's world number one Anse Young in the women's singles
final this afternoon. The match will be held at the Seyre Gwala Gagall complex in Paris, France,
with the winner crowned the French Open 2026 women's singles champion. Sindhu booked her place
in the final for the first time in her career after defeating Japan's Hina Akechi
in a thrilling three-game semifinal in Paris yesterday. At the inaugural FIFA
under-15 World Cup India defeated Cameroon to one to register their second consecutive
victory in Group K in Baku today.
